newsitem.title: USA: Rubin - must avoid inappropriate E-money regulation.
newsitem.headline: Rubin - must avoid inappropriate E-money regulation.

text.p: Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said on Thursday the United States must avoid "inappropriate regulation" of electronic money in order to allow the free flow of innovation.

Speaking to a conference on the future of electronic money, the term used to describe commerce that is largely transacted by computers, Rubin said a goal was to support its development and to make sure people feel confident about it.
"The last thing we want to do is to unnecessarily impede the development of innovations which are going to be so beneficial to our economy and our society," he said.

But he said electronic money poses difficult consumer protection issues, including avoiding monopoly, ensuring that adequate information to make choices was available, security was maintained and that issuers were financially sound.
There also were issues of counterfeiting, money laundering, piracy, civil fraud and the activities of computer hackers that merit attention, Rubin added.
Nonetheless, he said: "Government should protect consumers to the extent possible and enforce the law, but tread as lightly as possible."
Rubin announced at the conference, organized by the Treasury Department, that a consumer electronic task force was being set up to investigate issues arising from new payments systems.
He said the task force will include respresentatives from the Federal Reserve Board, the Federal Deposit Insurance Cop. the Federal Trade Commission and Treasury.
